content: The following information has been professionally translated into clear and concise medical language: Metabolism and Nutrition Disorders: Hypocalcemia may occur. Nervous System Disorders: Dysgeusia (altered taste perception) and paresthesia (abnormal sensations such as tingling or numbness) have been reported. Contraindications: Known heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). Known hypersensitivity to taurolidine, heparin, citrate excipients, or pork-derived products. Warnings and Precautions: Drug hypersensitivity reactions may occur. If a hypersensitivity reaction is observed, discontinue use and provide appropriate supportive care. This product is not intended for systemic administration. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: No animal reproduction studies have been conducted. Breastfeeding is not expected to expose the infant to the drug. Category A: Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk. Taurolidine: This is a thiazolidinone antimicrobial agent with broad-spectrum activity against gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, as well as mycobacteria. It also exhibits antifungal properties. Heparin: This anticoagulant inhibits activated coagulation factors involved in clotting, particularly factors Xa (at low doses) and IIa (at higher doses). It prevents the formation of a stable fibrin clot by inhibiting the activation of fibrin-stabilizing factor. Administration Instructions: This product is intended for instillation into central venous catheters (CVCs) only and is not for systemic administration. Do not use this product as a catheter lock flush solution. Withdraw the appropriate volume of catheter lock solution (CLS) from the vial using a sterile needle and syringe to fill the catheter lumens. Use a 3-mL or 5-mL single-dose vial, depending on the volume of the catheter lumens, to instill into each catheter lumen after every hemodialysis (HD) session. Before the next HD session, aspirate the taurolidine/heparin solution from the catheter and discard it. Each vial is designed for single use with a single patient and should be discarded after use. Storage Instructions: Store at controlled room temperature (20–25°C or 68–77°F), with permissible excursions to 15–30°C (59–86°F). Do not freeze. The product must remain in its commercial carton until it is instilled into the CVC. Additional Notes: Adding plans allows for comparison of formulary status with other drugs in the same class.
